text:
maria: noticing elevated job failures from us-east1-b GPU pool, roughly 18-22% failed over last 10m :rotating_light:
ashok: seeing the same — packet loss spikes to the egress gateway around 10:02 UTC, affected some heavy seq2seq batches
maria: can we isolate to specific subzone or instance type? any network ACL changes?
kevin: no infra ACL changes on record. Cloud provider reporting degraded transit in us-east1-b for certain host subnet ranges
jules: ok. plan: drain affected GPU instances from the pool, shift steady traffic to us-east1-c and us-west1 for non-low-latency jobs. will coordinate drain windows
maria: agree. how many instances do we have to drain? we need to avoid hitting Dedicated pool SLA or starving parked jobs
jules: about 24 N1-highmem GPU nodes in the affected AZ are showing >30% retransmits. we'll cordon and then drain 6 at a time to let autoscaler refill from other AZs
kevin: suggest routing policy change: prefer-region=us-east1-c for read/write and allow cross-region fallback for batch. raising cross-region burst capacity temporarily will cost but keeps jobs alive
ashok: oncall approve? @maria are you ok with the short-term cost delta?
maria: approve. prioritize customer-facing low-latency endpoints on dedicated pool, shift async batch to cheaper cross-region nodes. keep me posted on cost delta
jules: running drain command now:

```
# cordon and drain in batches
infractl node cordon --zone us-east1-b --label gpu_pool=general --selector "node-group=rg1" --limit 6
infractl node drain --grace-period 120 --evict-local-storage --zone us-east1-b --selector "node-group=rg1" 
```
ops-bot: [automated] Node cordon initiated for 6 nodes in us-east1-b by jules at 1769890105
deploy-bot: [automated] Routing policy updated: prefer-region us-east1-c for route /api/generate by jules at 1769890120
kevin: watching autoscaler, currently spinning 8 nodes in us-east1-c, ETA ~3m
ashok: telemetry shows token-serving latency for a small subset of requests still hitting us-east1-b due to cached route entries. flushing edge cache now
jules: flushed cache, re-evaluating traffic. starting next batch of 6 drains in 2m
maria: important — keep the Dedicated reserved pool untouched for critical endpoints. if we need capacity, prefer on-demand in other AZs first
kevin: noted. scaling policy adjusted: reserved-pool-min unchanged, flexible-pool-burst +8 across us-east1-c and us-west1 at 1769890285
ashok: after second batch, failed jobs dropped to ~3%. egress errors for the remaining nodes trending down
jules: final batch in progress, will mark nodes for reprovisioning after drain (network interface replacement)
ops-bot: [automated] Node drain complete for 18 nodes. Remaining 6 nodes under investigation at 1769890360
maria: good. open an incident ticket and link to postmortem. set incident severity P2 due to partial degradation and customer impact on batch jobs
ashok: opened inc-2026-042 in PagerDuty and created a brief runbook in the ticket with commands and metrics links
kevin: cost note: cross-region burst added ~0.7% monthly spend if sustained; documenting in ticket for finance review
jules: next steps: (1) reprovision network stacks on drained nodes (2) run soak for 24h on reprovisioned nodes (3) evaluate moving some cached routing to global LB with shorter TTL to avoid cache-stuck routes
maria: thanks team. keep updates in this thread and incident. will schedule a writeup for postmortem and cost impact estimate tomorrow :thumbsup:
kevin: monitoring alerting: create temporary panel for egress retransmits and failed-job ratio in datadog, shared link in ticket
ashok: will follow up with provider support for host-level NIC flaps, reference ticket #SR-998172
jules: marking thread as ops-complete for the immediate drain. leaving remediation and postmortem action items in the incident.
ops-bot: [automated] Incident inc-2026-042 created, severity P2, assigned to eng-infra at 1769890450 :white_check_mark:
